chapter: Road life, segregation and band pranks
title: How people viewed musicians and the Lunceford band's reputation
summary: Crawford says musicians were seen as an ordinary profession, but the Lunceford band, Ellington and Calloway were looked up to.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: How did people look at musicians then? I know you told me, one person told your wife that she shouldn't be messing around with a musician and a drummer at that, but that wasn't the way that people looked at musicians, was it?
No, what they thought of musicians was just an ordinary profession. That -- in other words, they weren't completely looked down on, unless they brought it about themselves.
Musicians in the Lunceford band were altogether different. They were looked up to, yeah, they were in a different category. That was a clean band.
Were there any other bands that were looked up to that you --

Duke Ellington. It all depended on on one musician and the personalities that different bands had. Other bands, oh, -- but Lunceford, Duke Ellington, and Cab Calloway got pretty popular there at one time, they were looked up to. There were something, struggling, other bands, they were looked down on.
What were the bands that were looked down on?

That I can't tell you. As a matter of fact, I just don't want to pinpoint them because I don't want to be in a libel suit or nothing like that. But there were many. I can name three that were looked up to.
